blocks.text: KATHMANDU — Nepal went to COP31 with the Bhotekoshi–Trishuli floods behind it and a plain ask: give mountains a permanent place in the UN climate talks. On October 29, Nepal and Bhutan jointly proposed a COP31 agenda item on “1.5°C warming in mountains”. It did not make the formal agenda. With negotiators now bargaining over the wording of the conference’s cover decision, Nepal is pressing for a dedicated mountain work program with a defined scope, an annual high-level dialogue, and finance that arrives on time. Avishek Shrestha, adviser to Minister for Agriculture, Forests and Environment Gita Chaudhary, is inside that process. […]... Keep on reading: Why did Nepal’s mountain agenda stall at COP31?
